name: Two-Row Recognition and Coefficient-Space Nerve
statement: When every terminal local system in exact coefficient reduction has at most two rows, positive logarithmic compatibility margin is equivalent to nonempty coefficient space, and $\mathcal A(C)$ is homotopy equivalent to the finite nerve of its feasible strict logarithmic cones. A collection of selections is a nerve face exactly when zero is outside the convex hull of its pooled inequality vectors, giving an exact rational linear-feasibility test. Singleton-disagreement terminal pairs, and empty terminal families, give contractible coefficient spaces whenever feasible.
proof: The two-row determinant criterion converts each terminal relation into a finite union of strict homogeneous linear systems in logarithmic coefficients. Exact reduction identifies their union with the coefficient space up to homotopy. All nonempty cone intersections are convex; the good-cover nerve theorem gives the homotopy equivalence, while strict separation of zero from the pooled convex hull gives the exact face test.
